You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test case "testExcelHeaderCountLessThanData" uses CSVFormat.EXCEL with a header line "A,B,C,," where the header line contains empty header names (empty columns at the end). The issue observed from the current bug report is that this produces an IllegalArgumentException due to duplicate empty header names.

Examining the code in CSVParser.initializeHeader() shows the logic that processes the header record:
- It reads the header record either from the CSVFormat header property or from the first line of the file.
- It then iterates over all header names in this header record.
- For each header name, it checks
  - if the header name already exists in the map
  - whether the header name is empty (null or trimmed empty string)
- If the header already exists in the map and is not empty, or empty but allowMissingColumnNames is false, it throws the IllegalArgumentException for duplicate headers.
- Otherwise, it puts the header and its index into the map.

This means that empty header names ("") are explicitly checked, and if getAllowMissingColumnNames() is false (likely the default), then duplicates of empty header names will cause the exception.

In the given test, the header line reads: A, B, C, "", "". So the empty header is repeated twice, causing the exception.

From the current description, the desired behavior is that the CSVFormat.EXCEL should ignore or allow empty header names that Excel inserts as blank columns so that this doesn't cause the duplicate header error.

Hence, the root cause is that in initializeHeader(), empty header names are treated as normal headers and duplicate empty headers cause this failure. This method does not currently ignore empty header names in the header line when building the header map if allowMissingColumnNames is false. The CSVFormat.EXCEL does not appear to override allowMissingColumnNames to true or have special behavior for empty header columns.

So to fix this, either CSVFormat.EXCEL needs to set allowMissingColumnNames to true, or initializeHeader() needs to be adjusted to ignore empty header names for duplicate checks or skip empty header names in this mode.

Recent bug reports do not directly mention this exact issue but there is one about empty header strings and null string causing NPE which links to similar header handling logic. That might be relevant for robust handling of empty strings in headers but not directly for duplicate detection.

Summary:
The failure occurs because initializeHeader() treats multiple empty header names as duplicates and throws IAE; this needs to be handled for CSVFormat.EXCEL which commonly has trailing empty header columns in exports from Excel. Current code does not ignore or specially treat empty header names for this format, hence the failure.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
